title: Claude Code: Auto Mode, Workflows & Session Orchestration (2026)
content:
## Overview

Since the original Claude Code Overview page was written, the permission model and multi-agent story evolved substantially. The single biggest shift is **auto mode**: a classifier that decides which tool calls are safe to run without a prompt, replacing the old binary of "approve everything" versus `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Alongside it, Claude Code gained script-driven multi-agent **workflows**, **cross-session messaging**, and **self-hosted cloud environments**. This page tracks how those shipped and what they do.

---

## Auto Mode

Auto mode replaces manual permission prompts with a classifier that runs in the background: safe actions execute immediately, risky ones still stop and ask. Its rollout was staged over several months:

- **March 23–27, 2026 (research preview)** — first shipped as an opt-in research preview.
- **May 18–22, 2026** — reached the Pro plan, supporting Sonnet 4.6 alongside Opus.
- **June 1–5, 2026** — extended to third-party providers (Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry) for Opus 4.7 and Opus 4.8, and gained safer defaults: it prompts before writing files that can execute code, and blocks destructive git commands you didn't ask for.
- **June 15–19, 2026** — began blocking transcript tampering and asks before `rm -rf` on unresolved shell variables.
- **July 13–17, 2026** — the opt-in variable requirement was dropped entirely on Bedrock, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry — auto mode just works there now.
- **August 14, 2026** — auto mode becomes the **default permission mode for new sessions** on Pro, Max, and Team plans, ending the research-preview era.

Auto mode's deny rules can also match on tool parameters, not just tool names — for example `Agent(model:opus)` denies spawning an Opus subagent specifically, while other models remain allowed.

---

## Dynamic Workflows

A **workflow** is a JavaScript orchestration script that fans work out to subagents deterministically — the pattern used for large reviews, migrations, and research sweeps that a single agent's context can't hold. A script defines `phase()` groups and composes `agent()`, `parallel()`, and `pipeline()` calls:

```js
export const meta = {
  name: 'review-changes',
  description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
}
const findings = await agent('Find bugs in the diff', { schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA })
const verified = await parallel(
  findings.bugs.map(bug => () => agent(`Verify: ${bug.title}`, { schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA }))
)
```

Workflows can orchestrate dozens to hundreds of subagents in a single run, with `pipeline()` avoiding artificial barriers between stages so independent items keep flowing instead of waiting for the slowest item in a batch. This shipped as part of the May 22–29, 2026 update cycle, alongside a **security-guidance plugin** that reviews Claude's own changes for vulnerabilities as it works.

---

## Cross-Session Messaging

Shipped August 3–7, 2026 (macOS and Linux): separate Claude Code sessions can now message each other directly. A coordinator session can hand a finding or a decision to another running session instead of the user having to copy context between terminals manually — useful when one session is deep in a long-running task and another needs to act on an intermediate result.

---

## Self-Hosted Environments

Also from the August 3–7 update: **self-hosted environments** let an organization run Claude Code cloud sessions on its own infrastructure rather than Anthropic-managed containers, in public beta on Team and Enterprise plans. This targets organizations with compliance or data-residency requirements that the standard cloud container model doesn't satisfy.

---

## Agent View and Session Management

- **`claude agents`** (Agent view, shipped May 11–15, 2026) opens a single screen listing every active Claude Code session — what's running, what's blocked waiting on the user, and what's finished.
- **Background subagents by default** (June 29 – July 3, 2026) — subagents run in the background automatically so the main session keeps working while they execute, rather than blocking on each one.
- **Sub-agents spawning sub-agents** (June 8–12, 2026) — background agent chains are supported up to five levels deep.
- **`/fork`** (July 13–17, 2026) copies the current conversation into a new background session while the original keeps going.

---

## Ultraplan and Ultrareview

Two cloud-assisted workflows target planning and review specifically:

- **Ultraplan** (early preview, April 6–10, 2026) drafts a plan in the cloud from the CLI, lets the user review and comment on it in a web editor, then runs it remotely or pulls it back to run locally.
- **`/ultrareview`** (public research preview, April 20–24, 2026; `claude ultrareview` CI/script access, April 27 – May 1, 2026) runs a fleet of bug-hunting agents in the cloud against a diff, with findings landing back in the CLI or Desktop automatically.

---

## Why It Matters

Together these changes move Claude Code from a single-agent, prompt-per-action tool toward a platform where multiple sessions and subagent fleets coordinate with less manual supervision — auto mode reduces interruption for routine actions, workflows scale a single task across many agents deterministically, and cross-session messaging plus self-hosted environments extend that coordination across machines and organizational infrastructure.
